scenes.title: The formal object
scenes.narration: Here is the formal object: subtract a target from zeta, then color the remaining phase. The colors classify output directions; they do not decide whether a zero exists. At a zero, the phase is undefined.
bullets: The output origin moves; the input axes stay fixed.
Four half-open phase sectors; retain the target label.
scenes.bubble: Define the object before interpreting the colors.
scenes.visual: Editable output-plane origin shifts to a. Four correct orientation sectors label phase directions; a white zero marker is explicitly undefined. Use an axis-boundary tag rather than assigning two colors.
scenes.sourceCredit: Phase plots: Wegert (2010) • Four sectors: display convention

scenes.title: What the computation supports
scenes.narration: Our finite computation found two paths leaving the original window and one reaching a one-point. Independent numerical checks support those observations. They do not certify every point between samples, and they do not show that the exiting branches disappear.
bullets: First detected exits; no interval certificate yet.
scenes.bubble: An exit from the picture is not an end to the mathematics.
scenes.visual: Reuse accepted paths at original scale. Mark two right-boundary exits and the Z3 endpoint; preserve old-target labels on held exit markers. Do not animate an uncomputed continuation beyond the viewport.
scenes.sourceCredit: Accepted 80-digit reference + native cross-check • Numerical evidence

scenes.title: A precise certificate to build
scenes.narration: The next precise task is to certify those three paths: prove uniqueness in overlapping boxes, exclude a zero derivative, and certify the two boundary crossings. That would turn selected numerical observations into a bounded mathematical certificate.
bullets: B₃ radius: 10⁻¹⁰. Fixed rational data; not yet certified.
Z1/Z2: certify first crossings in the fixed brackets.
scenes.bubble: The proof must cover the spaces between samples.
scenes.visual: Draw illustrative tube boxes around accepted paths. Use a prominent PROPOSED label: these are diagrams of future certificates, not actual interval enclosures. Check icons remain outlined/pending.
scenes.sourceCredit: Proposed bounded certificate • Not yet proved

scenes.title: Where this can be useful
scenes.narration: Boseman and Pauli already studied this continuation family. Complex target paths offer broader exploration. Speiser links Riemann to excluding derivative zeros throughout an entire half-strip. Our three paths do not cover that obligation; a global proof is still missing.
formulaLines: for every 0 < Re(s) < 1/2, at all heights
bullets: Finite tool validation; no RH proof or novelty claim.
scenes.bubble: Useful local evidence still needs a global argument.
scenes.visual: Small finite path window beside a strip extending beyond the frame in both height directions. Label critical values may be nonreal, and every height remains the global requirement. Keep source credit legible; no success mark on RH.

sources.title: Adam Boseman and Sebastian Pauli, On the zeros of zeta(s)-c
sources.use: Direct prior work on this same real-target continuation family from zeta zeros, including paths toward 1-points and rightward paths. Our finite viewport exits do not classify their eventual behavior.

sources.title: NIST DLMF 25.2, Definition and Expansions
sources.use: Dirichlet series for Re(s)>1 and meromorphic continuation with a simple pole at s=1.

sources.title: NIST DLMF 25.10(i), Distribution of zeros
sources.use: RH concerns all nontrivial zeta zeros at target zero.

sources.title: Norman Levinson and Hugh L. Montgomery, Zeros of the derivatives of the Riemann zeta-function
sources.use: Published Speiser equivalence: RH iff zeta prime has no zero in 0<Re(s)<1/2. Previously checked in the accepted prior-work audit; also stated on p. 137 of Boseman-Pauli.

sources.title: Elias Wegert, Phase Plots of Complex Functions: A Journey in Illustration
sources.use: Established phase-coloring foundation. Four half-open color sectors are this display convention, not a new theorem.

sources.title: S. J. Lester, a-Points of the Riemann zeta-function on the critical line
sources.use: Established research context for nonzero a-points; no distribution theorem from this paper is implemented here.

sources.title: Dave Platt and Tim Trudgian, The Riemann hypothesis is true up to 3*10^12
sources.use: Existing rigorous finite verification already includes our displayed heights; this experiment adds no verified RH height.
